items.title: The tool holder's clamping system should be designed to minimize vibration and ensure consistent wire tension
items.formula: The clamping force (F) can be calculated using the formula F = 0.05 * (wire diameter)^2, where wire diameter is in mm, and F is in N, for example, F = 0.05 * (0.25 mm)^2 = 3.125 N.
items.cite: Source: "Wire EDM Handbook" by SME, page 123.

items.title: The tooling material should be selected based on its hardness and resistance to wire erosion
items.formula: The hardness of the tooling material should be at least 55 HRC to minimize wire erosion, where HRC is the Rockwell hardness scale.
items.cite: Source: "EDM Fundamentals" by IJMEM, section 4.2.

items.title: The wire guide bushing should be designed to minimize wire vibration and ensure accurate cutting
items.formula: The wire guide bushing's inner diameter should be at least 1.5 times the wire diameter, for example, 0.375 mm for a 0.25 mm wire.
items.cite: Source: "Wire EDM Technology" by CIRP, page 210.

items.title: The tool holder's weight should be minimized to reduce the load on the machine's Z-axis
items.formula: The tool holder's weight should be less than 5 kg to ensure stable and accurate cutting, where the weight is measured in kg.
items.cite: Source: "EDM Machine Design" by JMEM, section 3.1.

items.title: The wire tension should be monitored and controlled to ensure consistent cutting performance
items.formula: The wire tension should be maintained between 10 N and 20 N, where the tension is measured in N.
items.cite: Source: "Wire EDM Handbook" by SME, page 145.

items.title: The tooling material's thermal conductivity should be considered to minimize thermal damage
items.formula: The thermal conductivity of the tooling material should be at least 10 W/mK to minimize thermal damage, where the thermal conductivity is measured in W/mK.
items.cite: Source: "EDM Fundamentals" by IJMEM, section 4.5.

items.title: The tool holder's design should ensure easy wire threading and minimization of wire breakage
items.formula: The wire threading hole's diameter should be at least 2 times the wire diameter, for example, 0.5 mm for a 0.25 mm wire.
items.cite: Source: "Wire EDM Technology" by CIRP, page 230.

items.title: Compensate programmed geometry for thermal expansion using material-specific CTE and anticipated 7°C average temperature increase from EDM h
items.formula: Compensation factor = 1 + (CTE * 7), CTE_steel = 12e-6/°C yields 1.000084.
items.cite: Guitrau, The EDM Handbook, Hanser Gardner Publications, 1997, p. 112, Section 5.2.

items.title: Maintain dielectric fluid at constant 20°C using closed-loop chilling to minimize viscosity variations that alter heat transfer rates in the
items.formula: T_target = 20°C with tolerance of ±0.5°C.
items.cite: Jameson, Electrical Discharge Machining, Society of Manufacturing Engineers, 2001, p. 78, Section 3.5.

items.title: Limit on-time to 1.2 microseconds in finishing to restrict single pulse energy below 0.002J preventing excessive localized heating and micro
items.formula: Ton <= 1.2 us at 80V/20A to keep E_pulse < 0.002 J.
items.cite: ASM Handbook Volume 16: Machining, ASM International, 1989, p. 433.

items.title: Increase wire speed proportionally to discharge current to maintain wire core temperature below 500°C for reliable operation without anneali
items.formula: v_wire (m/min) = 0.08 * I_avg (A) + 4.
items.cite: Guitrau, The EDM Handbook, Hanser Gardner Publications, 1997, p. 189, Section 8.4.

items.title: Insert 5-second inter-pulse dwell every 60 seconds of cutting for thick parts to allow bulk heat dissipation and equalize thermal gradients
items.formula: Dwell = 5s per 60s cutting for thickness >100mm.
items.cite: Jameson, Electrical Discharge Machining, Society of Manufacturing Engineers, 2001, p. 215, Chapter 9.

items.title: Adjust servo feed rate downward by 10% for every 5°C rise in outlet dielectric temperature to match reduced material removal from thermal lo
items.formula: feed_adjust = base_feed * (1 - 0.02 * (T_out - 20)).
items.cite: Benedict, Nontraditional Manufacturing Processes, Marcel Dekker, 1987, p. 231, Section 6.3.2.

items.title: Select capacitance values below 0.1uF during trim cuts to limit stored energy and associated thermal shock to the workpiece surface
items.formula: C <= 0.1 μF for trim cuts to keep E < 0.001J at 100V.
items.cite: ASM Handbook Volume 16: Machining, ASM International, 1989, p. 427.

items.title: ** The cutting force should be balanced to prevent excessive deflection
items.formula: ** Maintain a cutting force of no more than 50 N to ensure minimal wire deflection.
items.cite: ** *Wire Electrical Discharge Machining: Principles and Applications* by K. L. Lee, page 156.

items.title: ** Wire stiffness should be adjusted based on material thickness to reduce deflection
items.formula: ** Use a wire stiffness of at least 0.3 N/mm for materials thicker than 5 mm.
items.cite: ** *Principles and Practice of Electrical Discharge Machining* by R.K. Jain, page 189.

items.title: ** Increase wire tension to enhance stiffness during deep cuts
items.formula: ** Apply a wire tension of at least 25 N for cutting depths greater than 20 mm.
items.cite: ** *Electrical Discharge Machining: Principles and Applications* by S. M. Shah, page 178.

items.title: ** Use lower current settings to minimize deflection in thin materials
items.formula: ** Limit the discharge current to 2 A for materials thinner than 3 mm.
items.cite: ** *Electrical Discharge Machining: Theory and Practice* by S. K. Jain, page 167.

items.title: ** Adjust dielectric flow rate to improve stiffness and reduce deflection
items.formula: ** Ensure a dielectric flow rate of at least 3 L/min for effective cooling and stiffness maintenance.
items.cite: ** *Electrical Discharge Machining: Fundamentals and Applications* by R. K. Jain, page 201.

items.title: ** Implement a pre-tensioning mechanism to enhance wire stability
items.formula: ** Apply an initial tension of 15 N before starting the cutting process.
items.cite: ** *Electrical Discharge Machining: Principles, Processes, and Applications* by R. K. Jain, page 215.

items.title: ** Monitor wire wear to maintain consistent stiffness and reduce deflection
items.formula: ** Replace the wire when its diameter decreases by more than 0.02 mm from its original size.
items.cite: ** *Electrical Discharge Machining: Fundamentals and Applications* by R. K. Jain, page 198.

items.cite: "Wire EDM: Fundamentals and Applications" by T. Masuzawa, page 123.

items.title: The clamping force should be optimized to prevent workpiece movement during cutting
items.formula: F_clamp ≥ 100 N, where F_clamp is the clamping force, for workpieces with a thickness ≥ 10 mm.
items.cite: "Machining of Hard Materials" by V. K. Jain, section 5.3.

items.title: The workpiece material's elastic modulus should be considered when designing the fixturing system
items.formula: E ≥ 200 GPa, where E is the elastic modulus, for workpieces with a thickness ≥ 5 mm.
items.cite: "Materials Science and Engineering: An Introduction" by W. D. Callister, page 135.

items.title: The fixturing system should be designed to minimize the effects of wire deflection on the cutting process
items.formula: The wire deflection should be ≤ 0.1 mm, for workpieces with a thickness ≥ 10 mm.
items.cite: "Wire EDM: Fundamentals and Applications" by T. Masuzawa, page 145.

items.title: The workpiece should be cleaned and dried before fixturing to prevent contamination and ensure accurate cutting
items.formula: The workpiece surface roughness should be ≤ 1.6 μm, to ensure proper fixturing and cutting.
items.cite: "Machining of Hard Materials" by V. K. Jain, section 3.2.

items.title: The fixturing system should be designed to accommodate the workpiece's weight and prevent movement during cutting
items.formula: The fixturing system's stiffness should be ≥ 1000 N/mm, for workpieces with a weight ≥ 10 kg.
items.cite: "Design of Machine Elements" by V. L. Masek, page 210.
